usage: There is a TV in the living room.
I rest in the living room.
examples: My family talks in the living room.
The living room sofa is very comfortable.
I watch movies in the living room at night.
nuance: 거실 is the common shared space in a Korean home where family members gather, relax, and watch television together.
mistakes: Do not confuse 거실 with 침실 (bedroom).

usage: There is a bed in the bedroom.
examples: I read books in the bedroom.
The bedroom window is very big.
At night I rest well in the bedroom.
nuance: 침실 is the private room used mainly for sleeping, and it usually contains a bed and other personal furniture.
mistakes: Do not confuse 침실 with 거실 (living room).

usage: There are flowerpots on the balcony.
I dry laundry on the balcony.
examples: I grow plants on the balcony.
I look outside from the balcony.
There is a small chair on the balcony.
nuance: 베란다 is the outdoor extension of an apartment where Koreans often dry laundry, store items, or keep small plants.
mistakes: Do not confuse 베란다 with 마당 (yard).

usage: There are shoes at the entrance.
I take off my shoes at the entrance.
examples: We take off our shoes at the entrance.
There are two umbrellas at the entrance.
The guest waits at the entrance.
nuance: 현관 is the entryway of a Korean home where people remove their shoes before stepping into the main living space.
mistakes: Do not confuse 현관 with 대문 (front gate).

usage: There is snow on the roof.
A sound comes from the roof.
examples: That house has a very pretty roof.
When it rains the roof makes noise.
A bird is sitting on the roof.
nuance: 지붕 is the top covering of a building that protects the interior from rain, snow, and direct sunlight outside.
mistakes: Do not confuse 지붕 with 천장 (ceiling).

usage: There is a painting on the wall.
I hang a clock on the wall.
examples: I stick photos on the wall.
The wall color is very bright.
There is a big mirror on the wall.
nuance: 벽 is a vertical surface that divides rooms or encloses a space, and pictures or shelves are often placed on it.
mistakes: Do not confuse 벽 with 바닥 (floor).

usage: There is a bag on the floor.
examples: We sit on the floor and eat.
In winter the floor is warm.
I clean the floor every day.
nuance: 바닥 is the bottom surface of a room, and in Korea people often sit or sleep directly on the heated floor.
mistakes: Do not confuse 바닥 with 천장 (ceiling).

usage: There is a light on the ceiling.
examples: This room has a very high ceiling.
There is a pretty light on the ceiling.
I lie down looking at the ceiling.
nuance: 천장 is the upper inside surface of a room, the opposite of the floor, and lights are usually attached to it.
mistakes: Do not confuse 천장 with 지붕 (roof).

usage: There is a tree in the yard.
examples: The children run and play in the yard.
In summer we grill meat in the yard.
nuance: 마당 is the open outdoor ground around a house where families relax, dry crops, or hold small gatherings together.
mistakes: Do not confuse 마당 with 베란다 (balcony).

usage: There are flowers on the fence.
examples: The puppy plays inside the fence.
nuance: 울타리 is a low barrier that marks the boundary of a yard or garden and keeps animals and people apart.
mistakes: Do not confuse 울타리 with 벽 (wall).

usage: There is a number on the front gate.
I wait at the front gate.
examples: Grandma waits for me at the front gate.
I open the gate and enter the yard.
nuance: 대문 is the main outer gate of a house through which people enter from the street into the yard or property.
mistakes: Do not confuse 대문 with 현관 (entrance).
